summary.text: Jim Desmond, a Republican San Diego County supervisor, lost the November 3, 2026 election for the U.S. House seat in California's 48th District to Marni von Wilpert.

A former mayor of San Marcos, U.S. Navy veteran and retired Delta Air Lines pilot, he first launched a campaign in the 49th District, then ran in the 48th after Rep. Darrell Issa announced he would not seek re-election.
He ran on affordability, homelessness treatment and border security.

paragraphs.text: Desmond was born in Illinois and served in the U.S. Navy as an aircraft electrician from 1974 to 1979, then earned a pilot's license.
He graduated from San Diego State University with a bachelor's degree in electrical engineering in 1985 and founded a technical writing company, Technical Standards, Inc.
From 1986 to 2020 he flew for Delta Air Lines, piloting Boeing 757 and 767 aircraft, and he retired early in 2020; he describes himself as a retired Delta pilot.
Desmond served on the San Marcos City Council from 2004 to 2006 and was elected mayor of San Marcos in 2006, winning re-election unopposed in 2010 and 2014.
He won the District 5 seat on the San Diego County Board of Supervisors in 2018 and took office in January 2019, and was re-elected in 2022 with 60.1% of the vote.

In 2025 he launched a campaign against Rep. Mike Levin in the 49th District, then in 2026 announced a run for the 48th District after redistricting under Proposition 50; Rep. Issa, who is not seeking re-election, endorsed him.
According to Wikipedia, he is married with two children and lived in Oceanside as of 2022.
He received 40.7% of the vote to Marni von Wilpert's 59.3%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
